name: Squad formation grid
oneLiner: Each side fights as squads on a 2x3 grid: a front row that faces the enemy and a back row behind it. Melee can only reach the front row while anyone stands there; arrows and spells reach everyone and hit the back row harder; a melee fighter placed in the back strikes at half power. Before a fight a modal formation editor lets the player drag (mouse, touch) or key units between rows and squads, with the consequences spelled out per unit; the game's own battle calls targetsFor / pickTarget / hit for its target lists and damage. On a tactics map every unit token becomes a squad of members.
fits: turn-based party battle (side view or front view)
tactics / strategy RPG where map units become squads
squad-based strategy RPG with auto-resolved clashes (A-14 reuses the data model)
monster or unit collection games with a team-building screen
notFor: real-time action games (rows decide targets in a turn or an exchange)
games with one hero and no party
games where every attack must be able to reach every enemy (use backGuard: off, then rows only change damage)

needs: a fixed 60 Hz update step (the editor's only clock), also while the world is paused for it
the unit list per side: a unique id, HP, max HP, the reach of its normal attack (melee, ranged, magic) and a sprite
every place a target is chosen (player menu, tap hit test, enemy AI, autopilot) and every damage formula
where a battle (or wave, or map) starts and restarts, to build squads and open the editor
the direction keys and confirm / cancel routed to the editor while busy(); optional pointer events (attach)
optional: the game's autoplay flag, so the editor arranges and deploys by itself
provides: squads: {id, team, name, slots[6]} with front row = slots 0-2 and back row = 3-5 (the data model A-14 squad-clash builds on)
row rules: targetsFor(attacker, squad, reach), pickTarget(...) and hit(...) -> {ok, mul, why}; usable(unit, row) for row-locked skills
a modal formation editor (keyboard, mouse drag, touch, autopilot) with per-unit consequences and DEPLOY; onDone(squads) from update()
spot(unit, area): where each unit stands in a squad area (front row nearer the enemy)
in-world row tags, squad pips for map tokens, and guard marks while aiming

assets: module/squad-formation.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_SquadFormation): squad data model, pure row rules (also static via GameDNA_SquadFormation.rules), formation editor drawn on the game canvas through GameDNA_Skin (built-in pixel16 look), keyboard / pointer / autopilot input, row tags, pips and guard marks
no image or audio files (unit pictures come from the game)
